targets.old_statement: A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit, while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around.
targets.statement: A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit, while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around.

correction.corrected_statement: A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit, while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around.
correction.note: The missed exit rule appears on page 80, not page 79.

targets.old_statement: Dawn, dusk and bright oncoming lights call for low beams and a glance at the right road edge, while a single flash of the high beams is the only high-beam use against a glaring driver.
targets.statement: Before sunrise and after sunset you should turn on low-beam headlamps so others can see you, while if an oncoming vehicle's lights are too bright at night you should flash your high beams once and look toward the right edge of the road.

correction.corrected_statement: At dawn and dusk turn on low beam headlamps so others can see you, and at night if oncoming lights are too bright flash high beams once and look at the right edge of the road while using lane markings as a guide.
correction.note: Right edge glance applies only to bright oncoming lights, not to dawn and dusk.
